findings.title: Materials' 68-point lens gap signals earnings cliff
findings.body: Materials trades at a 68-point percentile gap between its trailing and forward multiples, the widest in the table, with forward earnings growth implied at 126 percent. That is the market pricing a dramatic earnings rebound that the trailing lens has not yet seen, a bet that looks unusually aggressive for a sector at the 20th percentile of its own five-year range.

findings.title: Energy's forward discount hides a rich trailing view
findings.body: Energy's forward P/E sits at the 37th percentile while its trailing multiple is at the 78th, a 41-point gap that implies 56 percent earnings growth ahead. The forward lens is calling for a sharp earnings recovery that the trailing lens has not confirmed, leaving the sector's apparent cheapness contingent on that growth actually arriving.

findings.title: Health Care's forward percentile hits 99 despite rich trailing
findings.body: Health Care's forward P/E is at the 99th percentile of its five-year range, while its trailing multiple sits at the 84th, with implied earnings growth of 86 percent. That near-maximum forward valuation is not just expensive on estimates; it is also pricing in a massive earnings jump that would need to materialize to justify the 46 percent multiple compression from trailing levels.
